# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Images RKE2 starts differently from what their config declares.
#
# entrypoint= REPLACES the ENTRYPOINT the image declares, which is what the
# container runtime does and what --roots cannot express: --roots adds a
# root and leaves the declared entrypoint rooted beside it.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Images this release starts more than one way. These get roots=, not
# entrypoint=.
#
# entrypoint= says "this image is started with this one command", which is
# false here -- and saying it twice is an error vexscan refuses ("named twice
# with different assertions; say it once"). roots= names every starting
# point and the closure is their union: a superset of any single container's,
# so it still fails closed.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# not run as a pod at all -- rke2 extracts its /bin onto the host and the host runs those binaries, so the roots are the binaries themselves

#   extracted to the host by rke2: /bin/kubelet
#   extracted to the host by rke2: /bin/runc

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What this generator will not decide for you.
#
# exec-policy=assume-none is the key that actually moves findings, and it is a
# claim nothing above is evidence for: "the program named here never starts
# another one". Add it per line, only where you believe it. Anything that is a
# supervisor (runit, tini, catatonit, s6) or a shell script is a no.
#
# Run without it first and read the exec-taint evidence -- vexscan names the
# symbols that made it suspect the binary can exec. A binary that links none of
# them needs no assertion at all.
#
# Say it once with a profile rather than on every line:
#
#   [profile single-binary] exec-policy=assume-none
#   <image>  profile=single-binary
#
# The name travels into the report and the emitted VEX -- "under the asserted
# runtime profile 'single-binary'" -- so a reviewer can look it up and disagree.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
